evals.name: project-save-load
evals.prompt: I'm implementing the .pixhaus file format in our `io` library crate. A project is serialized to MessagePack with rmp-serde and then compressed with zstd; these files can get large because we support 8K canvases. Write `save_project(project: &Project, path: &Path)` and `load_project(path: &Path)` for this. We use `thiserror` in library crates (no anyhow, no unwrap). Assume `Project: Serialize + DeserializeOwned`. Show the functions plus imports and any error enum you need. Explain the key choices briefly.
evals.expected_output: Streams MessagePack directly through zstd::stream::write::Encoder to the file and calls finish() (or auto_finish); load uses zstd::stream::read::Decoder + rmp_serde::decode::from_read. Uses thiserror, no unwrap. Bonus: notes compression level 3 / running off the UI thread via spawn_blocking.

evals.name: truncated-save-debug
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the Encoder is dropped without finish(), so the zstd frame epilogue (and buffered data) is never flushed, truncating the file. Fix: call encoder.finish()? before returning (or use auto_finish). Explains why small files might appear to work and why finish() is also where late I/O errors surface.

evals.name: thumbnail-cache-bulk
evals.prompt: While scrubbing the timeline we read and write a lot of small cached thumbnail tiles — about 800 of them, each a few KB of RGBA bytes. I want to zstd-compress each tile independently on the way to disk and decompress on the way back. Which zstd API fits this better than encode_all per tile, and why? Show compress and decompress helpers.
evals.expected_output: Recommends zstd::bulk::Compressor/Decompressor reused across the many small tiles (keeps the context/dictionary alive vs re-allocating per call). decompress takes a capacity bound. May suggest a trained dictionary (dict::from_samples + with_prepared_dictionary) since the tiles are small and similar. Correct API names.
